proposed.text: A building owner begins operating a new use in an existing building after only filing NBC Form B-12, without waiting for inspection or certificate issuance. Under PD 1096, which statement best describes the legal position?

options.text: Filing B-12 constitutes constructive notice and authorizes provisional occupancy pending final approval, allowing temporary use
The change of use is unauthorized; the building is being operated in violation of PD 1096 until the Certificate of Occupancy is issued
The owner is protected from enforcement action once B-12 is filed, as the BO's review is administrative only, not regulatory
The BO may only act after 30 days; the owner may operate in the interim without legal consequence, assuming compliance

proposed.rationale: Filing Form B-12 initiates the application process — it does not authorize the new use. Under Sec. 702, a change of use is only legally effective after the building conforms to Code requirements AND the Certificate of Occupancy is issued. Operating the new use before the Certificate of Occupancy is issued violates the Code, exposes the owner to administrative and criminal penalties, and exposes occupants to unverified safety risks.
proposed.explanation: Application filing ≠ authorization. The Certificate of Occupancy is the legal instrument that authorizes the new use — not the B-12 form. This is analogous to starting construction before a building permit is issued.
